course.description: You built something with Claude or Gemini — now what? This guide walks you through two practical paths to deploying your AI-built app online: Google AI Studio for fast, hosted prototypes in under 30 minutes, and GitHub + Netlify for full customization and deep integrations.
learningOutcomes: Apply the methods taught in How to Get Your AI-Built App on the Internet.

modules.description: Two paths to get your app live on the internet — fast prototype or full production.

lessons.content:
Claude (or another AI) just built you a working app — but it only runs locally on your computer. To share it with others or use it anywhere, you need to host it on the internet.

There are two main paths depending on your goal:

| Path | Best for | Time to deploy |
|------|----------|----------------|
| **Google AI Studio** | Fast prototypes, personal tools, demos | Under 30 minutes |
| **GitHub + Netlify** | Full customization, API integrations, production apps | 1–2 hours (first time) |

Read through both options and decide which fits your situation before starting.
lessons.title: Understand the problem

activities.title: Path A: Deploy with Google AI Studio (under 30 minutes)

lessons.content:
Google AI Studio has a built-in **Build mode** that lets you create and host an app directly from a prompt — no local setup required.

**Steps:**

1. Go to [aistudio.google.com](https://aistudio.google.com) and sign in with your Google account
2. Click **Build** (or open an existing project in Build mode)
3. Describe your app in the prompt box — paste your requirements or describe what you want
4. AI Studio generates the app with full-stack support (server-side logic, npm packages, secrets management)
5. Preview the app live in the browser — iterate by prompting further changes
6. When ready, click **Share** (top right) to get a shareable link — you can keep it private, share with specific people, or make it public
7. To make it permanently hosted, click **Deploy to Cloud Run** — this gives you a stable URL with Google's infrastructure behind it

**Cloud Run free tier:** 2 million requests/month — more than enough for personal tools and small teams.

**Tip:** Use this path for itinerary planners, coaching apps, fantasy sports tools, dashboards, or any single-purpose utility you want running in minutes.
lessons.title: Path A: Deploy with Google AI Studio (under 30 minutes)

activities.title: Path B: Deploy with GitHub + Netlify (full control)

lessons.content:
If your app has LLM integrations, API keys, a backend, or you want full customization — GitHub + Netlify is the right path. It's easier than it sounds, even if you've never shipped a website before.

**Steps:**

1. **Push your code to GitHub**
   - Create a free account at [github.com](https://github.com) if you don't have one
   - Create a new repository and upload your project files (or use `git push` if you're comfortable with the terminal)
   - Ask Claude: *"Help me push my local project to a new GitHub repo"* — it will walk you through it

2. **Connect to Netlify**
   - Create a free account at [netlify.com](https://netlify.com)
   - Click **Add new site → Import an existing project**
   - Select GitHub and authorize Netlify to access your repo
   - Choose your repository

3. **Configure the build settings**
   - Set the build command (e.g. `npm run build`) and publish directory (e.g. `dist` or `build`)
   - If unsure, ask Claude: *"What are the Netlify build settings for my project?"*

4. **Add environment variables**
   - In Netlify's site settings, go to **Environment Variables**
   - Add any API keys your app needs (never hardcode secrets in your code)

5. **Deploy**
   - Click **Deploy site** — Netlify builds and hosts it at a `yoursite.netlify.app` URL
   - Every future `git push` to your repo automatically redeploys the site

**Tip:** Use this path for RAG apps, apps with LLM API calls, multi-page sites, or anything that needs backend logic and persistent integrations.
lessons.title: Path B: Deploy with GitHub + Netlify (full control)

lessons.content:
Use this as a quick decision guide:

**Choose Google AI Studio if:**
- You want it live in under 30 minutes
- It's a personal tool, demo, or prototype
- No complex API integrations or backend required
- Examples: trip planner, coaching app, fantasy sports dashboard, quick calculator

**Choose GitHub + Netlify if:**
- Your app calls external APIs (OpenAI, Stripe, databases, etc.)
- You need a custom domain
- You want version control and automatic deploys on code changes
- You're building something production-grade or sharing with a team
- Examples: RAG chatbot, AI writing tool, business dashboard with live data

**Both are free to start.** You can always build fast in AI Studio first, then migrate to GitHub + Netlify once the idea is validated.

The best builders use both — prototype fast, then scale when it matters.
